rationale: The stated diagnosis — that the acquisition family's near-zero FMB slopes stem from rank-product tie mass — is contradicted by the archive itself, since "Buy Versus Build Investment Mix" was already a continuous, non-ranked aqc-minus-xrd ratio and still produced fmb -0.77, so this is a denominator swap on an already-tested specification rather than a fix for the diagnosed problem.

A genuine first crossing of the two most productive archive families (acquisition intensity × sustained-margin moat gate) with a coverage argument that is correct, though the low-margin leg risks simply re-expressing the gross-profitability anomaly and the template is the third reuse of the same margin gate.

Capital vintage (net/gross PP&E) is a genuinely new stock-based characteristic in this archive and the CMA-absorption argument is a sensible diagnosis, but the ratio is heavily contaminated by depreciation-policy and industry differences, and the R&D-rank gate reintroduces exactly the zero-mass problem the author dismissed as "uninformative" one proposal earlier.

Reversing the R&D gate from protective to risk-amplifying is a defensible and genuinely different asset-liability-matching claim, but the expression's natural direction is ambiguous because the high-R&D leg carries a well-documented positive return premium that fights the expected negative sign, and the high-leverage/high-R&D corner is sparse by construction.

Testing the impairment/realization stage rather than the spending stage is a legitimately new mechanism here, but the first leg is badly measured — NEG(DELTA(gdwl)) assigns a mid-to-high rank to the large mass of firms with zero goodwill change, mixing true impairers with non-acquirers — and post-impairment drift is already a documented accounting anomaly.

The margin-quality motivation for replacing sales growth with gross-profit growth is economically sound and the parent signal is the archive's only jointly strong long-side result, but this is a single-leg swap on two highly correlated growth measures and should be treated as a marginal refinement whose incremental value is likely small.
